jobs.title: CRNA Faculty with Assistant Program Director Appointment
jobs.description: CRNA Faculty with Assistant Program Director Appointment Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Posting Details WSU's Commitment to Equal Opportunity Weber State University is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating an environment welcoming to all individuals. We strive to create a culture where everyone feels valued and appreciated. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to protected categories, such as disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, race, religion, national origin, veterans status, or others, as required by law and university policy (see Weber State University's Policy and Procedure Manual 3-32). Position Information Position Title CRNA Faculty with Assistant Program Director Appointment Requisition Number F00533P Job Description Job DescriptionWeber State University’s Annie Taylor Dee School of Nursing is excited to announce an opening for a Certified Registered Nurse Anesthesiologist (CRNA) faculty member with an appointment as Assistant Program Director. This is a 12-month position that can be filled as either a tenure-track position or an instructor position with the option to move to a tenure-track position at a later date, depending on the candidate’s qualifications. While the candidate will initially be hired as a faculty member with an administrative appointment, the CRNA Assistant Program Director role is not necessarily a permanent part of this position as the role may rotate through the faculty within the department in the future.This faculty member appointment has primary responsibilities in teaching, student evaluation, and ongoing curriculum development within the nurse anesthesia program. This individual maintains an active teaching role, contributing to didactic, simulation, and/or clinical education. In addition to faculty responsibilities, the Assistant Program Director supports the Program Director in select administrative functions, including curriculum oversight, student recruitment, retention, and progression, while ensuring alignment with accreditation standards established by the Council on Accreditation of Nurse Anesthesia Educational Programs.In accordance with COA standards, the Assistant Program Director must be qualified to assume leadership responsibilities and acting authority for the program in the Director’s absence. This position collaborates closely with the Department of Nursing Graduate Studies Chair, WSU colleagues, and the School of Nursing administrative team. Job Duties Job Duties1. Teaching & Faculty Support Instruction: Provides didactic and clinical instruction within the program and promotes instructor development. Curriculum Evaluation: Completes program assessment reports and analyzes the effectiveness of the curriculum and faculty. Faculty Review: Contributes to annual faculty evaluations and collaborates with community partners to enhance the educational mission. 2. Clinical Management & Coordination Rotation Oversight: Manages student clinical rotations, ensuring all specialty rotation requirements and required case numbers are met for graduation. Site Relations: Acts as the primary liaison between clinical agencies and the University to maintain strong clinical partnerships. Clinical Evaluations: Oversees the evaluation of clinical sites and preceptors, ensuring the quality of the clinical learning environment. Site Visits: Conducts annual clinical site visits and maintains comprehensive clinical site records. Data Tracking: Manages the electronic case tracking system (e.g., Typhon) and reviews student monthly case records for accuracy and progress. Clinical Remediation: Identifies student performance issues in the clinical setting and coordinates remediation plans to support student success. 3. Program Leadership & Administration Accreditation: Assists the Program Director in preparing regulatory reports and ensuring continuous compliance with COA and specialty credentialing standards. Strategic Planning: Participates in strategic planning and the development of program and university policies. Governance: Helps organize the program’s committee structure and serves on program, college, and university committees. Admissions: Helps organize the student interview process and participates in the recruitment and orientation of high-quality applicants. Required Qualifications Required Qualifications: Doctoral Degree, must have graduated from an accredited CRNA nursing program Two years (minimum) of related experience as a CRNA Active Utah APRN license or be qualified for licensure in the state of Utah Basic technology skills – Experience with word processing and spreadsheets (Microsoft Office, Google Workspace), videoconferencing platforms (Zoom, Google Meet), and general database navigation Current CRNA clinical practice Preferred Qualifications Preferred Qualifications: Ability to communicate effectively Academic and teaching experience in higher education Project management skills Advanced technology skills, ability to integrate simulation technology into nursing education Experience with COA standards, policies, and procedures A successful candidate will be willing to Background Check? Yes Benefits Summary WSU offers a generous benefits package that includes medical, dental, long-term disability, life insurance, retirement, a wellness program with release time and paid incentives, tuition benefits, free tickets to athletic and performing arts events, and paid holidays. Full/Part Time Full Time Posting Detail Information Open Date 07/10/2026 Close Date Open Until Filled Yes Notes to Applicant If you are passionate about what you could offer and accomplish here at WSU, we would love to hear from you. The position comes with a generous benefits package.To apply, please complete the online application and attach a cover letter, transcripts, current CV, and the names and contact information for three professional references. jobs.description: Dean of Students Welcome from the Dean of Students Welcome to Westminster University. Whether you’re a currently enrolled student, an alum, or a family member or friend supporting a student, we are glad to have you as a part of our community. I can attest that Westminster is a very special place. It’s certainly a beautiful campus and our location in the Salt Lake valley is a great launching point for urban and wilderness adventures, but what truly makes Westminster special is the people: the students, staff, faculty, and the families and friends that together form a community of learners that genuinely care about each other and about making a difference in the world. While you’re here, I encourage you to lean into new experiences: Snag a free ticket to a performing arts event Enjoy a snack at the University-sponsored tailgate before cheering on one of our athletics teams Attend one of the many free lectures featuring world-renowned thought leaders that will challenge you to think differently As an institution of higher learning, Westminster wants to support and celebrate the growth you’ll experience while here. Maximizing your time at Westminster will require you to take [appropriate] risks, ask for help when needed, and offer help to others when you’re able. My role as the Dean of Students, and the purpose of our office, is to advocate for you and support your success. We can't wait to meet you soon. Go Griffins! Learn More About Student Care Student Care Navigating the college experience can be one of the most rewarding and challenging times in a student’s life. One of the best skills a student can learn while attending college is: How to advocate for themselves How to identify and access resources to support their well-being If you or someone you know is experiencing difficulties while attending Westminster, there are resources on campus to help. Integrated Wellness Students can access medical and mental health services in person with Integrated Wellness or online through Westminster's partnership with TimelyCare. The Purple Basket The Purple Basket addresses the impact of hunger, nutrition, housing insecurity, and disparities in access to basic needs. Students can access a variety of foods, as well as hygiene and household items, in the Purple Basket. If you're facing food insecurity and need additional support, you can find a list of local food resource centers. Submit a Report If you or someone you know may be experiencing a Title IX violation, you can submit a Title IX Incident Report. If you're concerned about another student, you can submit a Concerning Behavior Referral to alert a campus representative. Student Code of Conduct The Student Code of Conduct is updated annually and contains the institution's standards of behavior designed to uphold our pillars of honesty, reason, and respect. Read the Student Code of Conduct Title IX Westminster’s Title IX program is comprehensive and seeks to stop, remedy, and prevent incidents of gender-based discrimination and sexual misconduct. If you or someone you know may be experiencing a Title IX violation, this page will connect you to resources and the reporting form. Learn More About Title IX Parent and Family Resources If you are a member of a student’s support network, this page will connect you with monthly correspondence from the dean, as well as other useful campus resources for parents and families. Find Parent and Family Resources Institutional Safety Reporting As mandated by state and federal law, Westminster provides records of annual safety reports. View Institutional Safety Reporting Hazing Reporting View the latest federally-mandated Hazing Transparency Report. Report Hazing Drug and Alcohol Abuse Prevention Program Westminster provides a federally-mandated biennial DAAPP report. View DAAPP Reporting Dean's Advisory Council The Dean's Advisory Council (DAC) is a group of student leaders who work with the Dean of Students to create opportunities for strengthening the campus community and tackle issues that impact the student experience. DAC representatives serve as ambassadors for their fellow students, and their perspectives and input are highly valued and appreciated by the dean. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Any currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate student in good academic standing is eligible to serve on the DAC. Representatives are asked to attend 1 in-person meeting each month, attend events sponsored by the Dean of Students, and provide occasional input about issues that may impact students. For questions about the DAC, email Oliver Anderson (oanderson@westminsteru.edu). APPLY FOR THE DEAN’S ADVISORY COUNCIL Special Events Get connected with your fellow Griffins.
